Subject: AuroraAI dedicated capacity heatmap, isolation & SLA asks

Hi Claire / Aaron —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call earlier. Below is a concise recap (call highlights, confirmed pain, and a recommended standing configuration + next steps). Please flag anything I missed.

Call summary / confirmed pain points:
- Unpredictable tail latency during peak batches impacting realtime inference for Aurora Assist (customer-facing chat).
- Need for strict tenant isolation (PHI/health data) for the clinical features — you called this a hard requirement for any reserved pool.
- Bursty traffic around 09:00–11:00 PT and 20:00–22:00 PT; current infra spikes lead to throttling and queueing.
- SOC 2 / encryption (KMS) and audit logs required for procurement + legal.

Goals you stated:
- p95 latency <= 300ms on short prompts (<= 256 tokens) and predictable latency for long-tail loads.
- Dedicated capacity to avoid noisy neighbor variability and meet compliance controls.
- Proof of concept within Q3 (end of September) with an ops-ready runbook for go-live.

High-level recommended config (initial sizing heatmap attached):
- Baseline reserved pool: 4 x H100-equivalent nodes (quantized 4-bit runtime) configured as isolated lane (no multi-tenant co-location).
- Burst buffer: additional 2 nodes auto-burst for 2x peak for 2–5 minute windows.
- Autoscale policy: continuous batching with latency floor at 120ms to retain throughput efficiency; scale triggers at sustained queue > 150ms for 60s.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for common clinical templates to cut token cost by ~18% (we modeled this in the attached CSV).
- SLA targets we recommend for contracting: 99.95% availability for the reserved pool and latency SLOs p95 <= 300ms (short), p95 <= 750ms (long, >1024 tokens); can tighten after trial.

Attachments included: aurora_workload_heatmap.png (visual distribution by hour), AuroraAI_workload_snapshot.csv (sample traces), Mutual_Action_Plan_Aurora.docx (proposed milestones).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Sign off on the high-level sizing + prioritize technical deep-dive with SE (estimate 60–90 minutes).
2) Provide SOC2 questionnaire (you mentioned procurement has a form) — we can start collecting evidence in parallel.
3) Run a 2-week benchmark (we'll shadow your workload with a mirrored dataset) to validate latency and cost numbers.
4) Draft commercial terms and a 90-day trial SOW to align on credits and start date.

Estimated rough cost ballpark (very high-level): $XXk/month for baseline reserved pool (4 nodes) + burst licensing; we'll provide a firm estimate after reviewing sample traces.

If that looks right, Claire — can we schedule the technical deep-dive next week? Priyom (cc'd) will lead the bench and ops plan.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — solid writeup, appreciate the crispness. Couple quick clarifications: 

1) Procurement timeline: we are aiming to close vendor selections by the end of Q3. SOC2 evidence and contractual SLAs are gating.
2) Can you share a ballpark $/month for the 4-node baseline vs. 6-node (with burst)? We need a budget placeholder for the procurement packet.
3) For isolation: we require tenant-level encryption keys (customer-managed KMS) and audit log retention of 12 months. Is that supported in your private/dedicated offering?

Attaching the SOC2 questionnaire procurement asked us to fill out — it has some technical control boxes. If you can assign someone to help return that, that would be great.

Also, curious about the benchmark approach: will you mirror our traffic or run a synthetic? We prefer a mirrored run for accuracy but can discuss constraints.

Best,
Claire Benson
VP Product, AuroraAI
claire@auroraai.com

Subject: Re: AuroraAI dedicated capacity heatmap, isolation & SLA asks

Claire — thanks, and good questions. Short answers below, plus a concrete next-step plan.

On cost (ballpark):
- Baseline (4 H100-equivalent nodes, isolated lane): ~ $45k/month (includes runtime, ops, monitoring).
- Baseline + burst (6 nodes configured with 2-node burst buffer and autoscale): ~ $64k/month.
Note: final pricing depends on term length, burst burn rates, and any usage credits. We'll formalize in the commercial draft.

On isolation / compliance:
- Yes — Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and per-tenant audit logs with 12+ months retention. We also provide an exported evidence bundle for SOC 2 reports.

On benchmark approach:
- We prefer a mirrored-run (shadowing) of production traffic for the most accurate latency fidelity. If there are constraints, we can fall back to a replay of sanitized traces.

Proposed immediate next steps:
A) Technical deep-dive (60–90m) — Priyom will lead and collect any infra traces or access we need. Please propose 2 time slots next week; we'll run the mirrored-run playbook afterward.
B) Procurement: we'll complete the SOC2 controls mapping against your questionnaire and return a redline in 3 business days (Marissa will own the evidence pack).
C) Bench plan: 2-week mirrored run starting once the deep-dive items are complete. Bench will validate p95/p99 latency and cost delta for quantized runs.

Priyom / Marissa — can you confirm availability to run the deep-dive and own the SOC2 deliverable?

Claire / Aaron — if those steps look good, I'll kick off the HubSpot deal and send a proposed MAP and SOW.

Cheers,
Ben
